definition: A fixation point is the single external point at which both eyes are directed in normal vision. It is the point in the visual field that falls on the central part of the retina used for the sharpest seeing.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Fixationp; pinned source text

reasons: The packet states that the fixation point is the external point both eyes fixate in normal vision, but it does not explicitly describe the retina region as “used for the sharpest seeing.”

The packet specifies correspondence to “the stimulation of the centre of the fovea centralis,” and the provided definition’s “central part of the retina used for the sharpest seeing” goes beyond what is explicitly supported in the supplied text.

The second sentence adds unsupported material: the source says the fixation point corresponds to stimulation of the centre of the fovea centralis, but it does not state that this is the part of the retina used for the sharpest seeing.

The wording “point in the visual field” and “single external point” are close to the source, but the definition should stay within what the packet explicitly supports without adding interpretive gloss.
